title: Accenture Technology Vision 2014: Every Business Is a Digital Business: From Digitally Disrupted to Digital Disrupter
notes: Six trends, numbered 01-06. Labels are printed as 'Name: subtitle'; the name before the colon is the label, the subtitle is in the note. Research Methodology horizon is 'in the years ahead' (no fixed horizon). Published date from PDF creation date (2014-01-22).

entries.label: Digital–physical blur
entries.quote: The physical world is coming online as objects, devices, and machines acquire more digital intelligence.
entries.subject: Internet of Things and edge intelligence
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'Extending intelligence to the edge'.

entries.label: From workforce to crowdsource
entries.quote: Picture a workforce that extends beyond your employees: one that consists of any user connected to the Internet.
entries.subject: Crowdsourcing
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'The rise of the borderless enterprise'.

entries.label: Data supply chain
entries.quote: To truly unlock that value, companies must start treating data more as a supply chain, enabling it to flow easily and usefully through the entire organization—and eventually throughout each company’s ecosystem of partners too.
entries.subject: Enterprise data management

entries.label: Harnessing hyperscale
entries.quote: Eclipsed by more than a decade of innovation in software, the hardware world is again a hotbed of new development as demand soars for bigger, faster, lower-cost data centers.
entries.subject: Hyperscale data center hardware
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'Hardware is back (and never really went away)'.

entries.label: The business of applications
entries.quote: According to Accenture’s latest High Performance IT study, only 7 percent of applications currently reside in the cloud, and survey respondents expect that figure to approach 33 percent by 2020.
entries.subject: Enterprise apps and cloud applications
entries.metric: share of applications residing in the cloud (survey respondents' expectation)
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'Software as a core competency in a digital world'. Lead sentence: 'The way we build software is changing.' The number is a survey expectation from Accenture's High Performance IT study, quoted in the chapter.

entries.label: Architecting resilience
entries.quote: In the digital era, businesses must support wide-ranging demands for nonstop processes, services, and systems.
entries.subject: IT resilience
entries.note: Printed subtitle: '“Built to survive failure” becomes the mantra of the nonstop business'.
